newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Tenaga may not get more rate hikes soon.
newsitem.headline: Tenaga may not get more rate hikes soon.

text.p: Malaysian power utility Tenaga Nasional Bh may not get another rate hike in the next few years, Energy, Telecommunications and Posts Minister Leo Moggie said on Wednesday.
He said this was possible due to the fixing of gas prices for Tenaga at 6.40 ringgit/MMBTU up to the year 2000.
Moggie, speaking in the local Bahasa Malaysia language, said the government has "initiated a study for a future long-term tariff plan" to be conducted over the next few years.
Asked if Tenaga would be granted another rate hike while the study is being done, Moggie said,"we do not anticipate that." He added "That is why we have capped gas (prices)."
"A larger tariff increase was avoided through the capping of gas prices at the rate of 6.40 ringgit per mmBtu until the year 2000," the minister said.
Moggie said that price compares with around 7.0 ringgit per mmBtu (million British thermal units) at current prices.
